issues.body: The research record still hard-codes benchmark-style measurements throughout sections 6, 7, and 10, including opcode totals and percentages, package-level deltas, synthetic-chain results, corpus sizes, and test-run counts. The companion program record repeats those measurements in a table. Repository policy prohibits hard-coded performance numbers in Markdown and treats work-box measurements as non-canonical; labeling the figures non-canonical does not make embedding them compliant. This is materially the same major finding as round 3.
issues.fix_hint: Move raw opcode counts, percentages, package deltas, fixture results, corpus sizes, and other quantitative run measurements into the repository's approved generated/result artifact mechanism. Link that artifact from both changed Markdown files and retain only qualitative, evidence-bounded conclusions in the prose.
issues.title: Hard-coded performance measurements remain in Markdown

verdict.summary: Round 4 is stagnant. The same major repository-policy violation remains: both changed Markdown files embed extensive hard-coded performance and benchmark-style measurements, including opcode totals, percentages, per-package deltas, corpus and test counts, and synthetic-chain results. Calling the measurements non-canonical does not satisfy the explicit prohibition on hard-coded performance numbers in Markdown. Move quantitative results to the repository's approved generated/result artifact mechanism and leave only qualitative, evidence-scoped conclusions plus a link in these records.
